sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: In July 1798, an English poet visited the countryside on the banks of the River Wye.
sentences.zh: 1798年7月，一位英国诗人来到怀伊河畔的乡村。

sentences.en: On seeing the natural beauty of the area, William Wordsworth composed a poem.
sentences.zh: 看到当地的自然美景后，威廉·华兹华斯创作了一首诗。

sentences.en: It's titled, Lines Written a Few Miles Above Tintern Abbey.
sentences.zh: 诗名为《丁登寺几英里上方所写行脚诗》。

sentences.en: At one point, he describes the effect of the landscape on his psychological state.
sentences.zh: 在其中一处，他描述了风景对他的心理状态产生的影响。

sentences.en: He writes,
sentences.zh: 他写道，

sentences.en: These poets were sometimes given to literary excess.
sentences.zh: 这些诗人有时会流于文学夸张。

sentences.en: They felt things deeply, and they wrote effusively.
sentences.zh: 他们情感深刻，笔墨汪洋。

sentences.en: But more than two centuries after Wordsworth composed his poem,
sentences.zh: 但在华兹华斯创作这首诗两个多世纪后，

sentences.en: some scientists today are asking an unusual question.
sentences.zh: 如今的一些科学家提出了一个不同寻常的问题。

sentences.en: Were the romantics on to something?
sentences.zh: 浪漫主义者真的发现了什么吗？

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, in the final episode of our series, Happiness 2.0,
sentences.zh: 本周的《隐藏的大脑》，在我们“幸福 2.0”系列的最后一集中，

sentences.en: we look at what happens when we stop, really stop, to smell the roses.
sentences.zh: 我们将探讨当我们停下脚步，真正驻足去闻一闻花香时会发生什么。

sentences.en: For centuries, one of the central challenges in human behavior has been the problem of suffering.
sentences.zh: 几个世纪以来，人类行为的核心挑战之一就是痛苦的问题。

sentences.en: We all have aches and ailments, setbacks at work, and conflicts in personal relationships.
sentences.zh: 我们都有病痛、工作上的挫折以及人际关系中的冲突。

sentences.en: Many years ago, the psychologist Dakar Keltner found himself in a world of suffering.
sentences.zh: 很多年前，心理学家达舍尔·凯尔特纳发现自己置身于痛苦的世界中。

sentences.en: He was in his early 30s and had just moved from California to Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 他当时三十出头，刚从加州搬到威斯康星州。

sentences.en: What happened to me, Shankar, is I lived a life largely in California,
sentences.zh: 尚卡尔，我当时的经历是，我大部分的生活都在加州度过，

sentences.en: in the hills, in the mountains, in the oceans, in the culture, and so forth.
sentences.zh: 在山丘里、在群山中、在海洋旁、在文化氛围中，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And I went 2,000 miles away, and it was flat.
sentences.zh: 然后我去了2000英里外的地方，那里是一片平原。

sentences.en: And there were storms, and there was snow, and people rooted for the Packers,
sentences.zh: 那里有风暴，有雪，人们支持包装工队，

sentences.en: and they ate bratwurst, and there was no Mexican food, and the weather, and the cold.
sentences.zh: 他们吃小香肠，没有墨西哥菜，还有那里的天气和寒冷。

sentences.en: The cold rattled me.
sentences.zh: 寒冷让我感到不安。

sentences.en: I felt like Camus' stranger in a way, like I am in a strange land that I just physically,
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，我感觉自己就像加缪笔下的局外人，就像我在一个陌生的国度，仅仅从生理上、

sentences.en: temperature-wise, climate-wise, people-wise, I felt like a fish out of water,
sentences.zh: 温度上、气候上、人员上来说，我感觉自己像离水的鱼，

sentences.en: even though I look like somebody from Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 尽管我看起来就像个威斯康星人。

sentences.en: I'm, you know, of Northern European heritage.
sentences.zh: 我，你知道的，有北欧血统。

sentences.en: Dakar, who was just starting his career as a professor,
sentences.zh: 达舍尔当时刚开始教授生涯，

sentences.en: started to experience extreme bouts of anxiety.
sentences.zh: 开始经历极度的焦虑发作。

sentences.en: I come from a family on my mom's side that has a lot of anxiety,
sentences.zh: 我母亲家族这边有很多人都有焦虑症，

sentences.en: anxiety, and I started to have profound panic attacks,
sentences.zh: 焦虑，我开始出现严重的恐慌发作，

sentences.en: really beginning with the day that I departed to drive across the country to Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 真的从我开车横跨美国前往威斯康星州的那一天开始。

sentences.en: I had probably, I would say, 70 or 80 a year,
sentences.zh: 我想我大概一年有70或80次，

sentences.en: really technicolor, full-blown panic attacks.
sentences.zh: 那种非常真切、完全彻底的恐慌发作。

sentences.en: When I was teaching, when I would go see a movie to try to relax,
sentences.zh: 当我授课时，当我为了放松去看电影时，

sentences.en: when I would fly on an airplane to go to a conference,
sentences.zh: 当我坐飞机去参加会议时，

sentences.en: when I would hear from a colleague,
sentences.zh: 当我听到同事的消息时，

sentences.en: and it really caught me off guard, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 而且它真的让我措手不及，尚卡尔。

sentences.en: Like, wow, why am I feeling so estranged and anxious all the time?
sentences.zh: 就像，哇，为什么我一直感到如此疏离和焦虑？

sentences.en: Everything around Dakar seemed to remind him of his isolation.
sentences.zh: 达舍尔身边的每件事物似乎都在提醒他这种孤立感。

sentences.en: Everywhere he went, he experienced vulnerability.
sentences.zh: 他走到哪里，都体验到一种脆弱感。

sentences.en: He felt that his life was about to end.
sentences.zh: 他觉得自己的生命就要结束了。

sentences.en: My God, you know, for those people out in the audience who've had real panic attacks,
sentences.zh: 天哪，你知道的，对于听众中那些经历过真正恐慌发作的人来说，

sentences.en: they are spectacular, and they hit you,
sentences.zh: 它们非常强烈，向你袭来，

sentences.en: and you've literally, the brain says you're dying,
sentences.zh: 字面意思上，大脑告诉你你要死了，

sentences.en: and your body is telling you, you, Dakar Keltner, are dying,
sentences.zh: 你的身体在告诉你，你，达舍尔·凯尔特纳，快要死了，

sentences.en: and you're about to die right here.
sentences.zh: 你马上就要死在这里了。

sentences.en: It felt really solitary.
sentences.zh: 这感觉非常孤独。

sentences.en: And I remember there was this book about weird stories from Wisconsin
sentences.zh: 我记得当时有一本关于威斯康星州诡异故事的书，

sentences.en: about how anxious people ended up dying in Wisconsin
sentences.zh: 讲的是焦虑的人如何在威斯康星州最终死去，

sentences.en: because they would go out and start tilling the earth on their farm at two in the morning,
sentences.zh: 因为他们会在凌晨两点跑出去在农场的土地上耕作，

sentences.en: you know, and everything was frozen, and the guy froze to death.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，当时一切都冻住了，那家伙被冻死了。

sentences.en: And I was like, this is going to happen to me.
sentences.zh: 当时我想，这也会发生在我身上。

sentences.en: And it was happening to me.
sentences.zh: 而且它确实正在发生在我身上。

sentences.en: Dakar had moved across the country to join the University of Wisconsin,
sentences.zh: 达舍尔跨越全国加入威斯康星大学，

sentences.en: but his work provided no solace.
sentences.zh: 但他的工作并没有提供任何慰藉。

sentences.en: I was getting rejected for grants.
sentences.zh: 我的资助申请被拒绝了。

sentences.en: Papers were getting rejected.
sentences.zh: 论文被退稿了。

sentences.en: There was a conference on the social nature of emotion,
sentences.zh: 有一场关于情感社会属性的会议，

sentences.en: which is what I was writing about and defined my career on.
sentences.zh: 正是我一直在撰写并以此定义我职业生涯的领域。

sentences.en: I got rejected from.
sentences.zh: 我被拒绝参加了。

sentences.en: I started to dream about people broadcasting all the rejections of my papers and ideas and the like.
sentences.zh: 我开始梦见人们在广播我论文和想法的所有退稿通知之类的东西。

sentences.en: You know, I got a very mediocre to bad mid-career review.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我得到了一个非常平庸到糟糕的中期职业评估。

sentences.en: It was a real struggle, to be quite honest, and a lot of suffering.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，这是一场真正的挣扎，伴随着许多痛苦。

sentences.en: So like many of us who've been through something similar,
sentences.zh: 所以，就像许多经历过类似事情的我们一样，

sentences.en: you try to do a number of things to make yourself feel better.
sentences.zh: 你试图做很多事情来让自己感觉好一点。

sentences.en: At one point, you and some fellow academics banded together to form a basketball team.
sentences.zh: 有一次，你和一些同行学者联合起来组建了一支篮球队。

sentences.en: Tell me about that.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲那个吧。

sentences.en: Why did you do that, and how did it go?
sentences.zh: 你为什么要这么做，进展如何？

sentences.en: We formed this team that we named the Laughing Amygdala.
sentences.zh: 我们组建了一支名为“大笑杏仁核”的球队。

sentences.en: Because the Amygdala was all the rage at the time.
sentences.zh: 因为当时杏仁核非常火爆。

sentences.en: It was Joe Ledoux, the Amygdala, the Threat Center, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 那是约瑟夫·勒杜、杏仁核、威胁中心等等的时代。

sentences.en: And what was great about our team, Shankar, is we were all professors and three graduate students.
sentences.zh: 尚卡尔，我们球队最棒的地方在于，我们全都是教授加上三名研究生。

sentences.en: And we had this really unlikely team, and we won championships on the campus.
sentences.zh: 我们有着这支极不可思议的球队，并且赢得了校园锦标赛。

sentences.en: We beat the football team, you know, the fraternities.
sentences.zh: 我们击败了橄榄球队，你知道的，还有兄弟会。

sentences.en: And people were just stunned, you know.
sentences.zh: 人们都惊呆了，你知道的。

sentences.en: And so it was this magical run.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一段神奇的经历。

sentences.en: And, you know, Shankar, from the solitary life of 3 a.m., I would go to the gym and play.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，尚卡尔，从凌晨3点孤独的生活中，我会去健身房打球。

sentences.en: And basketball is five people flowing in motion in a sense of, you know, just we're all connected doing things together.
sentences.zh: 篮球就像是五个人在流动中配合，有一种，你知道的，就是我们所有人连在一起共同做事的感觉。

sentences.en: And when I'd walk to the gym, it felt like a sanctuary, that I would go there and leave behind the anxiety.
sentences.zh: 当我走向健身房时，它感觉像一个避难所，我去那里就能抛开焦虑。

sentences.en: I want to play a clip of music here, Dakar.
sentences.zh: 达舍尔，我想在这里放一段音乐片段。

sentences.en: It's from Raw Power, the 1973 album by Iggy Pop and the Stooges.
sentences.zh: 它来自伊吉·波普和讨好者乐队1973年的专辑《原始力量》。

sentences.en: Dakar, what memories does this music hold for you?
sentences.zh: 达舍尔，这段音乐对你来说有什么回忆？

sentences.en: Shankar, one of the, I think one of the deepest mysteries in science right now, in the social sciences,
sentences.zh: 尚卡尔，我认为目前科学界、社会科学界最深奥的谜团之一，

sentences.en: is why does music speak to us?
sentences.zh: 就是为什么音乐能触动我们？

sentences.en: And why does it speak to our soul?
sentences.zh: 为什么它能触及我们的灵魂？

sentences.en: And when I was in Madison, Wisconsin, I was really, you know, fighting and with anxiety and, you know, trying to find my way in life.
sentences.zh: 当我在威斯康星州麦迪逊时，我真的在，你知道的，与焦虑搏斗，并且，你知道的，试图在生活中寻找方向。

sentences.en: And at that time, I'd probably seen Iggy Pop, kind of a godfather of punk rock, about six to eight times.
sentences.zh: 在那时，我大概已经看过朋克摇滚教父伊吉·波普的演出六到八次了。

sentences.en: And he played, I think it was in Milwaukee.
sentences.zh: 他演出，我想是在密尔沃基。

sentences.en: And I took some friends to the show.
sentences.zh: 我带了一些朋友去看演出。

sentences.en: And it was just like basketball.
sentences.zh: 这就像打篮球一样。

sentences.en: Like, I was leaving behind the heat of anxiety of my academic life, my young career.
sentences.zh: 就像，我把学术生活、年轻职业生涯中焦虑的高温抛在了身后。

sentences.en: And I go to the show, and I get up close, and we're in this throbbing mosh pit that scientists now study.
sentences.zh: 我去看了演出，凑得很近，我们身处科学家现在正在研究的那个躁动的人群冲撞区中。

sentences.en: And he comes out, and he sings all his great songs, you know, Raw Power, and, you know, Lust for Life, and Passenger.
sentences.zh: 他走出来，唱了他所有的伟大歌曲，你知道的，《原始力量》，还有，你知道的，《对生活的渴望》和《乘客》。

sentences.en: I know them.
sentences.zh: 我都认识。

sentences.en: I'm singing.
sentences.zh: 我在跟着唱。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, at one point, he dives out into the crowd, and I'm right there, and I hold him, you know.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你知道的，有一次，他跳进人群中，我刚好就在那里，我抱住了他，你知道的。

sentences.en: And he's aloft on all of our hands.
sentences.zh: 他在我们所有人的手上高高举起。

sentences.en: And Shankar, I touch his skin, and his skin feels like God.
sentences.zh: 尚卡尔，我摸到了他的皮肤，他的皮肤感觉就像上帝一样。

sentences.en: You know, I'm just like, I can't believe I'm holding Iggy Pop's bicep.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我当时就想，我简直不敢相信我正抓着伊吉·波普的二头肌。

sentences.en: So, when I leave an Iggy Pop show, I'm drenched in sweat.
sentences.zh: 所以，当我离开伊吉·波普的演唱会时，我大汗淋漓。

sentences.en: I don't know who I am.
sentences.zh: 我不知道我是谁。

sentences.en: I'm embracing strangers.
sentences.zh: 我在拥抱陌生人。

sentences.en: And I feel alive and pure.
sentences.zh: 我感到充满生机和纯粹。

sentences.en: So, I go back to Wisconsin, and I look at his CD, and it says,
sentences.zh: 所以，我回到威斯康星州，看着他的CD，上面写着，

sentences.en: If you feel like writing me, drop me a line.
sentences.zh: 如果你想写信给我，给我留个信吧。

sentences.en: Here's my address.
sentences.zh: 这是我的地址。

sentences.en: So, I write him, you know, and I tell him about all my stories, you know, of seeing him and how important he's been to me as a young professor, handling my struggles.
sentences.zh: 所以，我写信给他，你知道的，我告诉了他我所有的故事，你知道的，关于看他演出，以及作为一个年轻教授处理我的挣扎时，他是多么重要。

sentences.en: Six months later, I get a letter back in this little shaky scrawl, and it's like, he says,
sentences.zh: 六个月后，我收到了一封回信，上面是颤抖的小字，就像是，他说，

sentences.en: Thanks for all of your stories.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你所有的故事。

sentences.en: I really appreciate them.
sentences.zh: 我真的很感激。

sentences.en: Good luck getting access to the young skulls at UW.
sentences.zh: 祝你在威斯康星大学接触到那些年轻的大脑时好运。

sentences.en: I dig teachers, Iggy Pop.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢老师，伊吉·波普。

sentences.en: And I, like, I'm getting goosebumps talking about this now.
sentences.zh: 而我，就像，现在说起这个我都起鸡皮疙瘩。

sentences.en: Like, I held the letter, and I'm like, my life's okay.
sentences.zh: 就像，我拿着那封信，心想，我的生活没问题。

sentences.en: I have courage and strength.
sentences.zh: 我有勇气和力量。

sentences.en: And when I'd bounce up on the stage and teach my 300 students, getting my mediocre reviews and making mistakes here and there, I felt more strong and alive.
sentences.zh: 当我在舞台上蹦蹦跳跳地给300名学生上课，拿到平庸的评价并在各处犯错时，我感到更加强大和充满生机。

sentences.en: You were touched by the hand of God here, Dekker.
sentences.zh: 达舍尔，你在这里被上帝之手抚摸了。

sentences.en: The godfather of punk rock.
sentences.zh: 朋克摇滚的教父。

sentences.en: Another time, Dekker, you and your wife were outside watching a summer storm approach.
sentences.zh: 还有一次，达舍尔，你和你的妻子在外面看着一场夏日风暴逼近。

sentences.en: Tornado warnings were going off.
sentences.zh: 龙卷风警报拉响了。

sentences.en: Describe for me what was happening, and tell me what you both did next.
sentences.zh: 请为我描述当时发生了什么，并告诉我你们俩接下来做了什么。

sentences.en: My wife, Molly, grew up in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 我的妻子莫莉在旧金山长大。

sentences.en: You know, we both were adapting to the weather and the climate and the landscape.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们都在适应天气、气候和风景。

sentences.en: And this storm starts rolling in, and you could see it from afar, and those clouds looked horrifying, and they looked strong and dangerous.
sentences.zh: 然后这场风暴开始滚滚而来，你可以从远处看到它，那些云看起来很吓人，它们看起来强劲而危险。

sentences.en: And then there was some kind of warning that said, get into your basement, a tornado warning.
sentences.zh: 然后有一些警告说，进入你的地下室，这是龙卷风警报。

sentences.en: And I think tornadoes did land that day.
sentences.zh: 我想那天确实有龙卷风着陆了。

sentences.en: And for whatever reason, we said, let's feel it.
sentences.zh: 出于某种原因，我们说，去感受它吧。

sentences.en: Let's get out in the storm.
sentences.zh: 让我们走到风暴中去。

sentences.en: Let's see what the mystery is.
sentences.zh: 让我们看看奥秘是什么。

sentences.en: And let's just, you know, we couldn't really explain it.
sentences.zh: 让我们，你知道的，我们其实解释不清。

sentences.en: But we sat out on our swing, on our front porch, as this wild storm ripped through, you know, Madison for half an hour or whatever it was, and rain and lightning and massive winds.
sentences.zh: 但当这场狂暴的风暴肆虐麦迪逊半小时或无论多久时，我们坐在前廊的秋千上，雨水、闪电和巨大的狂风交加。

sentences.en: And again, it felt, I just felt so alive and free of the shackles of my anxiety at the time.
sentences.zh: 再次，这种感觉，我当时感到如此充满生机，摆脱了焦虑的枷锁。

sentences.en: So it was a striking experience.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一次令人震撼的经历。

sentences.en: So these all seem like very different experiences, enjoying teamwork in a basketball game, being part of a crowd at a music concert, watching a storm approach.
sentences.zh: 所以这些看起来是非常不同的体验，在篮球比赛中享受团队合作，在音乐会上成为人群的一部分，观看风暴逼近。

sentences.en: Is there a common thread that connects these experiences, Dakar?
sentences.zh: 达舍尔，有没有一条共同的线索将这些经历联系在一起？

sentences.en: You know, it was really interesting, Shankar, because I was really struggling in these four years.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这真的很令人有趣，尚卡尔，因为在这四年里我真的很挣扎。

sentences.en: And I, you know, I was chronically anxious, tons of panic attacks, struggling career-wise, really feeling away from home.
sentences.zh: 而且我，你知道的，我长期焦虑，有大量的恐慌发作，职业生涯举步维艰，真的有一种离家的感觉。

sentences.en: And I didn't know how to find happiness, which has been a life's puzzle for me in many ways.
sentences.zh: 我不知道如何寻找幸福，这在许多方面一直是我人生的谜题。

sentences.en: And I think what I was doing in these experiences is I was, I was getting outside of myself on the basketball court.
sentences.zh: 我想我在这些经历中所做的是，我在球场上超越了自我。

sentences.en: It's just the motion and the physicality and the, you're playing with five people.
sentences.zh: 这只是运动、体能以及，你和五个人一起打球。

sentences.en: I was losing myself and I lost myself right up front, like in a mosh pit near seeing Iggy Pop and feeling the music.
sentences.zh: 我迷失了自我，我就在最前沿迷失了自我，就像在伊吉·波普演出附近的冲撞区感受音乐那样。

sentences.en: And I lost myself in the storm, you know, I was just like, I was throwing myself into things where I could lose myself.
sentences.zh: 我在风暴中迷失了自我，你知道的，我只是，我把自己投入到能让我迷失自我的事物中。

sentences.en: Like William Wordsworth two centuries ago, Dakar had begun to discover ways out of his narrow preoccupations.
sentences.zh: 就像两个世纪前的威廉·华兹华斯一样，达舍尔开始找到摆脱狭隘执念的方法。

sentences.en: When we come back, the connections between these different experiences and the science behind a mind-expanding emotion.
sentences.zh: 稍后回来，我们将探讨这些不同体验之间的联系，以及拓展思维的情绪背后的科学。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 您正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: University of California, Berkeley psychologist Dakar Keltner studies what he calls prosocial emotions, feelings like love, compassion, and gratitude.
sentences.zh: 加州大学伯克利分校的心理学家达克尔·凯尔特纳一直在研究他所谓的“亲社会情绪”，比如爱、同情和感恩。

sentences.en: Earlier in his life, he tried to get himself through a difficult time by immersing himself in sports, in music, and in the beauties of the natural world.
sentences.zh: 在他年轻的时候，他曾试图通过全身心投入运动、音乐以及大自然的美景中来度过难关。

sentences.en: In time, he realized there was a common connection between these activities.
sentences.zh: 渐渐地，他意识到这些活动之间存在着某种共同的联系。

sentences.en: They all activated a feeling of being awestruck.
sentences.zh: 它们都唤起了一种心生敬畏的感觉。

sentences.en: Now at the University of California, Berkeley, Dakar has spent years studying the science of awe.
sentences.zh: 如今在加州大学伯克利分校，达克尔已经花了好几年时间来研究敬畏科学。

sentences.en: Dakar, I want to talk about your scientific explorations of awe, but so much of your intellectual journey starts with your personal journey.
sentences.zh: 达克尔，我想聊聊你对敬畏的科学探索，但你的许多学术探索其实都始于你的个人经历。

sentences.en: Both your parents were attuned to the world of art.
sentences.zh: 你的父母都对艺术世界有着敏锐的感知。

sentences.en: Can you tell me about them?
sentences.zh: 能跟我讲讲他们吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, you know, it's funny.
sentences.zh: 对，你知道，这挺有意思的。

sentences.en: I really lived a life that really is, in some sense, from my first moments of being born in Mexico, a life as an experiment in awe.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，我的人生从我在墨西哥出生的那一刻起，就像是一场关于敬畏的实验。

sentences.en: Formative years in Laurel Canyon, California, in the late 60s, so much music going on, Joni Mitchell, The Doors.
sentences.zh: 60年代末，我在加利福尼亚州的桂冠峡谷度过了成长的岁月，那里有太多的音乐，有琼尼·米歇尔、多门乐队。

sentences.en: My dad was a painter, and he loved awe-inspiring, horrifying work.
sentences.zh: 我父亲是一名画家，他热爱那些令人敬畏、甚至有些惊悚的作品。

sentences.en: Goya, Velasquez, Francis Bacon, and others, right?
sentences.zh: 比如戈雅、委拉斯开兹、弗朗西斯·培根等等，对吧？

sentences.en: Just as a kid, I was just seeing images all the time.
sentences.zh: 我从小到大，眼前总是能看到这些图像。

sentences.en: And then my mom loved awe in literature, and was getting her PhD, eventually taught at Cal State Sacramento, and loved, you know,
sentences.zh: 然后我母亲热爱文学中的敬畏感，当时她正在攻读博士学位，后来在加州州立大学萨克拉门托分校教书，她很喜欢，你知道的，

sentences.en: Virginia Woolf and her awesome portrayals of the mind and the romanticism and Wordsworth and Blake.
sentences.zh: 弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫以及她对心灵和浪漫主义的出色刻画，还有华兹华斯和布莱克。

sentences.en: And I would hear quotes of Blake, and she told me about the prelude of Wordsworth and, you know, and then also D.H.
sentences.zh: 我会听到布莱克的一些名句，她还会跟我讲华兹华斯的《序曲》，你知道的，还有D.H.

sentences.en: Lawrence and others.
sentences.zh: 劳伦斯等人的作品。

sentences.en: And so my parents were pointing me at an early age, from like five and six, like, here are quotes about awe, here are paintings of awe, here is music.
sentences.zh: 所以我的父母在我很小的时候，比如五六岁时，就在引导我，比如：这里有关于敬畏的名言，这里有敬畏的画作，这里有音乐。

sentences.en: You know, I remember listening to Sgt.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我记得自己曾听过中士

sentences.en: Pepper's when it came out, The Beatles, together as a family.
sentences.zh: 佩珀专辑的发行，那是披头士乐队的歌，全家人一起听的。

sentences.en: Like, life's about awe, go do it.
sentences.zh: 就像是，人生就是为了体验敬畏，去感受它吧。

sentences.en: Woke up, fell out of bed, dragged a comb across my head.
sentences.zh: 醒来，滚下床，拿梳子划过头顶。

sentences.en: Found the way downstairs and drank a cup.
sentences.zh: 找到下楼的路，喝了一杯。

sentences.en: I understand that your family moved to a rural community in the foothills of the Sierras, and you and your brother, Rolf, spent many days roaming outside in nature.
sentences.zh: 我听说你们家搬到了内华达山脉山麓的一个乡村社区，你和你的兄弟罗尔夫在野外大自然中度过了很多时光。

sentences.en: You know, it was incredible.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，那太不可思议了。

sentences.en: My parents, you know, it was 1970, my mom had just gotten this job at Cal State Sacramento as an English professor, teaching romanticism and the like.
sentences.zh: 我父母，你知道，那是1970年，我母亲刚在加州州立大学萨克拉门托分校找到了一份英语教授的工作，教授浪漫主义文学之类的课程。

sentences.en: And they did what a lot of people did in that era, is they moved to the country where it was cheaper, and we got an old, beat-up Victorian, five acres,
sentences.zh: 他们做了那个时代很多人都会做的事，搬到了比较便宜的乡下，我们买下了一栋破旧的维多利亚式老房子，占地五英亩，

sentences.en: and there were streams and creeks and ponds and railroad tracks we could follow, you know.
sentences.zh: 那里有我们可以沿着走的溪流、小溪、池塘和铁轨，你知道的。

sentences.en: And we just wandered after school.
sentences.zh: 放学后我们就到处闲逛。

sentences.en: We didn't do any homework.
sentences.zh: 我们不写任何家庭作业。

sentences.en: And then as we got older, what we started to do, Shankar, is go to the rivers, you know, rafting, and then in particular to the Yuba River, which is this wild river,
sentences.zh: 后来随着年龄的增长，尚卡尔，我们开始去做的事情是去河里，你知道的，玩漂流，尤其是去尤巴河，那是一条狂野的河流，

sentences.en: and jump into it.
sentences.zh: 然后跳进去。

sentences.en: And so I had this incredible childhood of biking and walking out in the country.
sentences.zh: 所以我度过了一个不可思议的童年，骑着自行车，在乡间漫步。

sentences.en: We lived on a dirt road where when I'd go walk home from the school dance, it was pitch black.
sentences.zh: 我们住在一个泥土路上，当我从学校舞会步行回家时，四周漆黑一片。

sentences.en: And I'd see this giant sky of stars, shooting stars.
sentences.zh: 我能看到巨大的星空，还有流星。

sentences.en: We slept outside, you know, so it was about wild awe.
sentences.zh: 我们睡在室外，你知道的，所以那是一种狂野的敬畏。

sentences.en: So that brings me to a question that I've been pondering for a bit in this conversation, which is that awe in general seems like an ineffable emotion.
sentences.zh: 这就引出了一个我在这次对话中一直思考的问题，那就是敬畏感总体上似乎是一种难以言表的情绪。

sentences.en: It feels like it's very hard to wrap your arms around what exactly it is.
sentences.zh: 感觉很难准确说清楚它到底是什么。

sentences.en: And if you're going to study it scientifically, you have to know what it is that you're studying.
sentences.zh: 如果你要对它进行科学研究，你就必须知道你所研究的究竟是什么。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So about 20 years ago, I understand that you and a collaborator came up with a working definition of awe.
sentences.zh: 所以大约20年前，我听说你和一位合作者提出了一个关于敬畏的工作定义。

sentences.en: Can you tell me how that came about?
sentences.zh: 能跟我讲讲这是怎么来的吗？

sentences.en: It seems ineffable and beyond words, but yet people really want to talk about it.
sentences.zh: 它似乎难以言表、无法用言语形容，但人们却真的很想谈论它。

sentences.en: It's mysterious and numinous, and we probably can measure it.
sentences.zh: 它神秘而神圣，而且我们大概可以测量它。

sentences.en: And that's one of the tasks of science.
sentences.zh: 这也是科学的任务之一。

sentences.en: So Jonathan Haidt, who is an early collaborator in my career and brilliant mind, we got invited to write a paper for a special issue on pleasure.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森·海特是我早期的合作者，也是个才华横溢的人，我们当时应邀为一期关于“快乐”的特刊写一篇论文。

sentences.en: And John and I had been talking about awe.
sentences.zh: 我和乔恩一直在讨论敬畏。

sentences.en: And we said awe, the key elements are when we encounter vast mysteries that we can't understand with our current knowledge.
sentences.zh: 我们当时说，敬畏的关键要素在于，当我们遇到用现有知识无法理解的巨大神秘时。

sentences.en: Or what we said was awe requires what we call the need for accommodation.
sentences.zh: 或者我们当时说，敬畏需要我们所说的“顺应需求”。

sentences.en: You have to rearrange your knowledge structures just to make sense of what you've encountered.
sentences.zh: 你必须重新调整你的知识结构，才能理解你所遇到的事物。

sentences.en: But I think for our conversation today, it's really awe is encountering vast mysteries that we don't understand.
sentences.zh: 但我认为对于我们今天的对话来说，敬畏实际上就是遇到我们无法理解的巨大神秘。

sentences.en: So nature is very often a common source of awe for many people.
sentences.zh: 所以大自然对很多人来说，往往是敬畏的共同来源。

sentences.en: I want to play for you an audio clip.
sentences.zh: 我想放一段音频给你听。

sentences.en: This is from a video made by a man named Paul Vasquez.
sentences.zh: 这是保罗·瓦斯克斯这个人制作的一段视频。

sentences.en: His nickname is Bear.
sentences.zh: 他的绰号是“熊”。

sentences.en: He saw something outside his home in Yosemite.
sentences.zh: 他在优胜美地的家外面看到了某种东西。

sentences.en: Whoa!
sentences.zh: 哇！

sentences.en: Whoa!
sentences.zh: 哇！

sentences.en: Whoa!
sentences.zh: 哇！

sentences.en: Oh my God!
sentences.zh: 我的天哪！

sentences.en: Oh my God!
sentences.zh: 我的天哪！

sentences.en: Oh my God!
sentences.zh: 我的天哪！

sentences.en: It's full on double rainbow all the way across the sky!
sentences.zh: 横跨整个天空的全景双彩虹！

sentences.en: Oh my God!
sentences.zh: 我的天哪！

sentences.en: So, Dacher, you've seen this video, I believe.
sentences.zh: 那么，达克尔，我相信你看过这个视频。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: As a scientist, would you care to hazard a guess at what's happening inside Paul Vasquez's mind at that moment?
sentences.zh: 作为一名科学家，你愿意斗胆猜测一下那一刻保罗·瓦斯克斯的脑海里在发生什么吗？

sentences.en: This video is really what mystical experiences are like for people.
sentences.zh: 这个视频真实地展现了人们所经历的神秘体验。

sentences.en: They laugh.
sentences.zh: 他们会笑。

sentences.en: They use language that is expansive and beyond the usual kinds of terms we use.
sentences.zh: 他们使用的语言十分宏大，超出了我们平时使用的那些词汇。

sentences.en: It's full on.
sentences.zh: 太震撼了。

sentences.en: It's, oh my God!
sentences.zh: 天哪，我的老天！

sentences.en: We cry.
sentences.zh: 我们会哭泣。

sentences.en: We are moved outside of ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我们的思绪被带到了自我之外。

sentences.en: You know, I want to play you a clip from the end of the same video, Dacher,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，达克尔，我想放一段同一视频结尾的片段给你听，

sentences.en: because it brings up something that I want to ask you about.
sentences.zh: 因为它引出了一个我想向你请教的问题。

sentences.en: Oh my God!
sentences.zh: 我的天哪！

sentences.en: What does it mean?
sentences.zh: 这意味着什么？

sentences.en: What does it mean?
sentences.zh: 这意味着什么？

sentences.en: What does it mean?
sentences.zh: 这意味着什么？

sentences.en: Too much!
sentences.zh: 太强了！

sentences.en: I doubt what it means!
sentences.zh: 我真不敢相信这意味着什么！

sentences.en: You know, it's interesting, Paul is almost uncomfortable by the intensity of the experience.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这很有趣，保罗甚至对这种强烈体验感到有些不适。

sentences.en: He's struggling to understand what it means.
sentences.zh: 他正费力地想要理解这究竟意味着什么。

sentences.en: And I think when most people think about awe, they think about, okay, I'm seeing something beautiful.
sentences.zh: 我想大多数人在想到敬畏时，会认为，好吧，我看到了美好的事物。

sentences.en: I see a beautiful sight.
sentences.zh: 我看到了美丽的风景。

sentences.en: But I think we're getting into deeper waters here where awe can actually make us uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们正在探讨更深层次的东西，敬畏其实会让我们感到不适。

sentences.en: Yeah, you know, awe destabilizes.
sentences.zh: 是的，你知道的，敬畏会打破平衡。

sentences.en: It introduces profound uncertainty about our understanding of the world.
sentences.zh: 它会给我们的世界观带来深刻的不确定性。

sentences.en: It can be filled with threat.
sentences.zh: 它可能充满了威胁感。

sentences.en: You know, when I sat amidst a storm, you know, I felt threatened.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当我坐在风暴之中时，你知道，我感到了威胁。

sentences.en: Just recently I was backpacking with my daughter Natalie High Sierras and we got caught in a lightning storm.
sentences.zh: 就在最近，我和女儿娜塔莉一起在内华达山脉高地背包徒步，我们遭遇了一场雷暴。

sentences.en: And it was awe-inspiring and threatening.
sentences.zh: 那既令人敬畏又充满威胁。

sentences.en: And that is true, I believe, with Vasquez's experience, the double rainbow experience.
sentences.zh: 我相信瓦斯克斯的经历，也就是双彩虹的经历，也是如此。

sentences.en: You know, when we no longer can make sense of reality, which is a theme of awe, it's that mystery, it's the need for finding new understandings of the world.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当我们无法再理解现实时——这是敬畏的一个主题，那种神秘感，那种寻找对世界的新理解的需求——

sentences.en: Often we feel adrift, we feel anxious, we feel threatened, and we feel destabilized.
sentences.zh: 通常我们会感到迷失、焦虑、受到威胁，并且内心平衡被打破。

sentences.en: You found that another realm of experience that tends to inspire awe involves other people who do amazing things.
sentences.zh: 你发现另一种往往能激发敬畏感的体验领域，涉及那些做出惊人行为的其他人类。

sentences.en: Tell me about the idea of moral beauty, Dakar.
sentences.zh: 能跟我讲讲道德美的概念吗，达克尔。

sentences.en: You know, moral beauty is the idea that other people's kindness and courage and overcoming obstacles in their virtuosity and their discipline can inspire us morally,
sentences.zh: 你知道，道德美是指其他人的善良、勇气、克服逆境的精神、精湛的技艺以及纪律，能够在道德上激励我们，

sentences.en: where we see in them what we want to be as good human beings.
sentences.zh: 我们在他们身上看到了我们作为优秀人类所渴望成为的样子。

sentences.en: And it astonished us, Shankar, at the Berkeley Lab that, you know, we sent out these requests, 26 countries, all these stories of awe come rolling in.
sentences.zh: 尚卡尔，这让我们伯克利实验室的人感到惊讶，我们发出这些征集后，来自26个国家的各种关于敬畏的故事纷至沓来。

sentences.en: And the most universal and the most common was the goodness or moral beauty of other people right around them.
sentences.zh: 而最普遍、最常见的就是他们身边其他人的善良或道德美。

sentences.en: And I'm not talking about Mahatma Gandhi or Mother Teresa.
sentences.zh: 我说的不是圣雄甘地或特蕾莎修女。

sentences.en: It is like neighbors and strangers and grandmothers and the like and roommates that, almost on a weekly basis, are triggering us to feel like, God, people are good.
sentences.zh: 就像邻居、陌生人、祖母之类的人，还有室友，他们几乎每周都在触发我们产生这样的感觉：天哪，人们真好。

sentences.en: And I could be inspired by that.
sentences.zh: 我可以从中受到启发。

sentences.en: I understand that you once had a powerful experience with a spiritual leader that also inspired a feeling of awe.
sentences.zh: 我听说你曾与一位精神领袖有过一次深刻的经历，那也激发了你对敬畏的感觉。

sentences.en: Tell me about your encounter with the Dalai Lama.
sentences.zh: 能跟我讲讲你与达赖喇嘛的会面吗？

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: It makes me humble to talk about it.
sentences.zh: 谈起这个让我感到很谦卑。

sentences.en: You know, I've been on two panels with His Holiness the Dalai Lama.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我曾和尊者达赖喇嘛一同参加过两个小组讨论。

sentences.en: And I'm like, man, I'm on a stage with the Dalai Lama.
sentences.zh: 当时我想，天哪，我和达赖喇嘛同台了。

sentences.en: And there are 2,500 people out in the audience.
sentences.zh: 台下坐着2500名观众。

sentences.en: Before we go on, I greet His Holiness.
sentences.zh: 在我们上台之前，我向尊者致意。

sentences.en: It's a profound moment.
sentences.zh: 这是一个深刻的时刻。

sentences.en: When he looks you in the eye, man, you feel like he is really looking me in the eye.
sentences.zh: 当他看着你的眼睛时，老兄，你会觉得他真的在直视我的眼睛。

sentences.en: And we hugged.
sentences.zh: 我们拥抱了。

sentences.en: And he kind of tickled me.
sentences.zh: 他还顺便逗了我一下。

sentences.en: And I was and I literally I was one giant goosebump.
sentences.zh: 我当时……字面意义上，我浑身起满了鸡皮疙瘩。

sentences.en: You know, I was like, wow, I've just hugged and been tickled by the Dalai Lama.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我当时想，哇，我刚刚和达赖喇嘛拥抱了，还被他逗了一下。

sentences.en: Then we go on stage and, you know, and I'm asking him these dumb questions.
sentences.zh: 然后我们上台了，你知道，我竟然在问他那些愚蠢的问题。

sentences.en: And, you know, the narrow scientists.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我是个狭隘的科学家。

sentences.en: And he's so engaged and interested and curious, you know, because he's training his mind in a way.
sentences.zh: 但他却那么投入、那么感兴趣、充满好奇，你知道的，因为他在以某种方式训练自己的心灵。

sentences.en: He's working harder on his mind than I've ever worked on anything.
sentences.zh: 他在修炼心性上所付出的努力，超过了我这辈子在任何事情上付出的努力。

sentences.en: And at one moment in this conversation, I'm asking him about compassion.
sentences.zh: 在这次对话的某个时刻，我问他关于同情心的问题。

sentences.en: And he says, compassion is the natural state of the mind.
sentences.zh: 他说，同情心是心灵的自然状态。

sentences.en: And I, you know, coming out of my Western scientific homo economicus mindset, I was just it was it was an epiphany.
sentences.zh: 我呢，带着西方科学“经济人”的心态，当时就觉得——这简直是一次顿悟。

sentences.en: And epiphanies are a very subtle source of all where suddenly we grasp that there are big ideas that really make sense of a lot of things in reality.
sentences.zh: 顿悟是敬畏的一种非常微妙的来源，突然之间我们领悟到，有一些宏大的理念真正赋予了现实中许多事物以意义。

sentences.en: You might find epiphanies in the idea of free markets or evolution or that capitalism is bad for the planet or big data or the idea of quantum physics.
sentences.zh: 你可能会在自由市场、进化论、资本主义对地球有害的观点、大数据或量子物理学的概念中发现顿悟。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it's surprisingly common around the world and has this structure to seeing suddenly being revealed to big ideas that help you make sense of the mysteries that concern you.
sentences.zh: 这在世界各地出奇地普遍，并且具有这样一种结构：突然豁然开朗，接触到那些宏大的理念，帮助你理清那些困扰你的神秘事物。

sentences.en: And it was an awe moment.
sentences.zh: 那是一个充满敬畏的时刻。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I was like, wait a minute.
sentences.zh: 我当时想：等一下。

sentences.en: Compassion is the deepest structure in the human mind down in the midbrain.
sentences.zh: 同情心是人类心灵深处最底层的结构，位于中脑之中。

sentences.en: All these structures that have been part of mammalian evolution.
sentences.zh: 所有这些结构都是哺乳动物进化过程的一部分。

sentences.en: And that animated a lot of research I did on compassion and change how I teach.
sentences.zh: 这激发了我对同情心的大量研究，并改变了我的教学方式。

sentences.en: And it changed how I thought about humanity, you know, that there is this deep goodness in us that's part of our evolutionary story.
sentences.zh: 它改变了我对人类的看法，你知道，原来我们体内存在着这种深厚的善良，这是我们进化故事的一部分。

sentences.en: That's one of the most interesting parts of our evolutionary story, how good we are.
sentences.zh: 这是我们进化历程中最有趣的部分之一，那就是我们有多么善良。

sentences.en: And it blew my mind.
sentences.zh: 这让我大开眼界。

sentences.en: You know, you talked about going to see Iggy Pop and then feeling like you could go on stage, you know, and talk to 300 students with newfound confidence.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你曾谈到去看伊吉·波普的演出，然后感觉自己可以带着全新的自信上台去给300名学生演讲。

sentences.en: Did you find the same thing happened after meeting the Dalai Lama?
sentences.zh: 你发现见过达赖喇嘛后也有同样的感受吗？

sentences.en: Did your life feel different in the days and weeks that followed?
sentences.zh: 在接下来的日子和星期里，你觉得你的生活有什么不同吗？

sentences.en: After that experience with His Holiness the Dalai Lama, I felt like I had a deeper sense of purpose and meaning.
sentences.zh: 在与尊者达赖喇嘛有过那次经历后，我感觉自己拥有了更深层次的目标感和意义感。

sentences.en: And so, you know, I'm on an airplane and I had profound flight anxiety.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我在飞机上，我以前有严重的飞行焦虑。

sentences.en: Every little bump felt like the end of my life.
sentences.zh: 任何一点颠簸都让我觉得像是世界末日。

sentences.en: I'd have images of losing my life and my children and so forth.
sentences.zh: 我的脑海里会浮现出失去生命、失去孩子之类的画面。

sentences.en: And I noticed that I wasn't anxious on the flight.
sentences.zh: 我注意到我在这次飞行中并不感到焦虑。

sentences.en: I didn't need to power down a whiskey to make it home, you know.
sentences.zh: 我不需要狂灌威士忌来撑着回家，你知道的。

sentences.en: And then I got there and I was at the carousel.
sentences.zh: 然后我到达了目的地，站在行李提取转盘旁。

sentences.en: And of course, my luggage was loSt.
sentences.zh: 当然，我的行李丢了。

sentences.en: And I literally laughed it off.
sentences.zh: 而我简直是付之一笑。

sentences.en: And I think I said, good, you know, time to shed all that stuff.
sentences.zh: 我想我当时说，太好了，你知道的，是时候抛掉所有这些杂物了。

sentences.en: I truly felt, and this is true of the science of awe, which is the mundane things don't get to you as much.
sentences.zh: 我由衷地感到——敬畏科学也是如此——那就是世俗琐事不会对你产生那么大的影响了。

sentences.en: And I felt above them and strong.
sentences.zh: 我感到自己超脱了它们，并且内心强大。

sentences.en: So I think, you know, all of us have had these experiences where we have that warm glow we get from, you know, an encounter with an awe-inspiring person or an experience.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，你知道的，我们所有人都曾有过这样的体验：当我们与一个令人敬畏的人相遇，或经历某种体验时，内心会涌起那种温暖的光芒。

sentences.en: Is there any risk, Thacker, that this can act, you know,
sentences.zh: 达克尔，会不会有这样一种风险，就是这可能会起到一种，你知道的，

sentences.en: like a kind of drug that we get a high from feeling awestruck and inspired and then this can lead us to be complacent or even oblivious to the sorrows or horrors of the world?
sentences.zh: 类似于毒品的作用，让我们从对敬畏和灵感的感受中获得亢奋，进而导致我们变得自满，甚至对世界的悲伤或恐怖视而不见？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think there are many risks of awe, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为敬畏有很多风险，对吧？

sentences.en: This is a destabilizing emotion.
sentences.zh: 这是一种会打破平衡的情绪。

sentences.en: It leads you to look for new knowledge to make sense of the world.
sentences.zh: 它会引导你去寻找新的知识，来理解这个世界。

sentences.en: It leads you to abandon past knowledge structures, perhaps, or assumptions.
sentences.zh: 它可能会引导你抛弃过去的知识结构，或者假设。

sentences.en: And, you know, a parent might think of, well, that's what happened to my daughter when she joined a cult.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，父母可能会想，嗯，我的女儿加入邪教时就是这样的。

sentences.en: As this cult leader suddenly persuaded her to abandon life and follow this new awe-inspiring figure, you know, there's a new concern in the psychedelic movement of,
sentences.zh: 当这位邪教领袖突然说服她放弃生活并跟随这个崭新的、令人敬畏的人物时，你知道的，迷幻剂运动中出现了一种新的担忧：

sentences.en: for certain people who find too much, you know, destabilizing search for new meaning in psychedelic experiences, it can get them into trouble.
sentences.zh: 对于某些人来说，他们在迷幻体验中发现了太多、你知道的、旨在寻找新意义的、破坏平衡的探索，这可能会给他们带来麻烦。

sentences.en: You could go on.
sentences.zh: 你可以继续说下去。

sentences.en: P.R.
sentences.zh: 公关

sentences.en: Carlo Valdesolo has, you know, nice studies showing that certain kinds of awe make us see kind of patterns where there aren't patterns.
sentences.zh: 卡洛·瓦尔德索洛（Carlo Valdesolo）的研究，你知道的，非常精彩，表明某些种类的敬畏会让我们在原本没有规律的地方看到规律。

sentences.en: And so we can believe things.
sentences.zh: 因此我们可能会相信一些事情。

sentences.en: You know, maybe a QAnon supporter feels goosebumps and awe at these stories that are absolute nonsense.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，也许一个“匿名者Q”（QAnon）的支持者听到这些完全是无稽之谈的故事时，也会起鸡皮疙瘩并感到敬畏。

sentences.en: They don't have a sense of boundaries.
sentences.zh: 他们没有边界感。

sentences.en: They enter into dangerous situations.
sentences.zh: 他们陷入了危险的境地。

sentences.en: So, yeah, there are risks here that we should be attentive to.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这里确实有我们需要注意的风险。

sentences.en: As there are, Shankar, with every human passion.
sentences.zh: 正如人类的每一种激情一样，香卡，这是必然存在的。

sentences.en: So, you've become increasingly interested in the evolutionary origins of awe.
sentences.zh: 所以，你对敬畏的进化起源越来越感兴趣了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Why is it that we would have an emotion like this?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们会拥有这样一种情绪？

sentences.en: You know, it's possible that other species also experience awe.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，其他物种也可能体验到敬畏。

sentences.en: But, of course, you know, we don't typically see a line of cats sitting and watching the sunset together, right?
sentences.zh: 但是，当然，你知道的，我们通常不会看到一排猫坐在一起看日落，对吧？

sentences.en: It just doesn't happen.
sentences.zh: 这种事根本不会发生。

sentences.en: So, is there something that might explain our predisposition to awe from an evolutionary perspective?
sentences.zh: 那么，有什么东西可以从进化角度解释我们对敬畏的倾向吗？

sentences.en: You know, this is where the science of awe gets really interesting, which is how far back in our primate mammalian evolution can we trace this, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这就是敬畏科学变得非常有趣的地方，那就是我们可以把这种情绪追溯到灵长类和哺乳动物进化的多远以前，对吧？

sentences.en: If it is a basic emotion.
sentences.zh: 如果它是一种基本情绪的话。

sentences.en: And we have a lot of data that suggests awe is as basic to humanity and the human species as anger or fear.
sentences.zh: 我们有大量数据表明，敬畏对于人类和人类物种的重要性，就像愤怒或恐惧一样基础。

sentences.en: And we have a lot of data on the expression of awe and what it does to our social behavior and sense of self that awe is this pretty deep human universal emotion.
sentences.zh: 我们有大量关于敬畏的表达、它对我们的社会行为和自我意识的影响的数据，表明敬畏是一种相当深厚的人类普遍情绪。

sentences.en: And I think that it does two things that are vital to our evolution.
sentences.zh: 我认为它对我们的进化至关重要地做了两件事。

sentences.en: And the first is it connects the individual to collectives.
sentences.zh: 首先，它将个人与集体联系起来。

sentences.en: And time and time again, when people experience awe, they see things like,
sentences.zh: 一次又一次，当人们体验到敬畏时，他们会说出这样的话：

sentences.en: I felt small and I felt like I was part of something larger than myself.
sentences.zh: 我感到自己很渺小，并且觉得自己是比个体更宏大的事物的一部分。

sentences.en: And this is fundamental to our survival.
sentences.zh: 这对于我们的生存至关重要。

sentences.en: And then the other thing that I think is really important, Shankar, is that awe helps us see the systems around us and understand them.
sentences.zh: 然后我认为非常重要的一点是，香卡，敬畏帮助我们看到周围的系统并理解它们。

sentences.en: One of the sets of operations of our mind is to be very narrow and focus on the self and individual actions and cause and effect relationships.
sentences.zh: 我们大脑的一套运作方式是非常狭隘的，专注于自我、个人行动以及因果关系。

sentences.en: The other is to look at the world holistically and systemically.
sentences.zh: 另一套则是以整体和系统的眼光看待世界。

sentences.en: That's an ecosystem.
sentences.zh: 那是一个生态系统。

sentences.en: This is a social hierarchy.
sentences.zh: 这是一个社会等级。

sentences.en: That is a musical structure.
sentences.zh: 那是一个音乐结构。

sentences.en: And awe pops those systems out to our awareness.
sentences.zh: 而敬畏将这些系统凸显到我们的意识中。

sentences.en: So it really is the animator of a systems view of life.
sentences.zh: 所以它确实是生命系统观的激活者。

sentences.en: And that's really important for scientific understanding, for social understanding, for knowing where to find resources in my environment, right, to understand my ecology.
sentences.zh: 这对于科学理解、社会理解、了解在我的环境中哪里可以找到资源来理解我的生态，真的非常重要，对吧？

sentences.en: And awe is the great engine of a systems view of the world.
sentences.zh: 敬畏是世界系统观的伟大引擎。

sentences.en: You know, and so much of it begins with the feeling that awe can produce in us of making us feel small.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这一切很大程度上始于敬畏在我们体内产生的一种让我们感到渺小的感觉。

sentences.en: I remember visiting Alaska once and feeling like I was a very small creature on a very, very big planet.
sentences.zh: 我记得有一次去阿拉斯加参观，感觉自己是一个在一个非常、非常巨大的星球上的极其微小的生物。

sentences.en: And you've done studies looking at the same idea.
sentences.zh: 你也做过探讨相同观点的研究。

sentences.en: You ran an interesting study in Yosemite exploring this idea that awe changes our sense of our own scale.
sentences.zh: 你在优胜美地进行了一项有趣的研究，探讨了敬畏会改变我们对自己尺度感知的观点。

sentences.en: You know, the self takes up a lot of area in the brain and in our consciousness.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，自我在大脑和我们的意识中占据了很大的面积。

sentences.en: We're always thinking, especially in this modern world, about my goals, my status, my aspirations, what I'm doing.
sentences.zh: 我们总是，尤其是在这个现代世界里，在考虑我的目标、我的地位、我的抱负、我在做什么。

sentences.en: It's my desires, my interests.
sentences.zh: 全都是我的欲望，我的兴趣。

sentences.en: And evolutionists have really talked about the problem of self-intereSt.
sentences.zh: 进化论者确实讨论过自私的问题。

sentences.en: How do we get people to orient to other people, to societies and collectives?
sentences.zh: 我们如何让人们去面向他人、面向社会和集体？

sentences.en: And we started to have this idea that awe does that by creating the small self.
sentences.zh: 我们开始有这样一种想法，即敬畏通过创造一个渺小的自我来做到这一点。

sentences.en: In a lot of writings about awe, right, religious writings from centuries ago, nature writings, Ralph Waldo Emerson, his big epiphany, I am nothing, right?
sentences.zh: 在许多关于敬畏的著作中，对吧，几个世纪前的宗教著作、自然文学、拉尔夫·沃尔多·“爱默生”的巨大顿悟——我什么也不是，对吧？

sentences.en: Psychedelic writings.
sentences.zh: 迷幻剂著作。

sentences.en: Psychedelic writings.
sentences.zh: 迷幻剂著作。

sentences.en: All these writings are speaking to this, but we had to get it empirically.
sentences.zh: 所有这些著作都在讨论这一点，但我们需要通过实证来获得它。

sentences.en: So my collaborator, Yang Bai from China, went to Yosemite, stopped travelers from 42 countries at this particular outlook on a road where you first get to see Yosemite Valley.
sentences.zh: 所以我的合作者，来自中国的杨白，去了优胜美地，在路上一个能首次看到优胜美地山谷的特定观景台上，拦住了来自42个国家的游客。

sentences.en: And El Capitan and the great granite slabs and this incredible valley that's just awe-inspiring.
sentences.zh: 还有酋长岩、巨大的花岗岩石板，以及这个令人惊叹的山谷，它简直令人敬畏。

sentences.en: And what Yang Bai did is she did a really simple task.
sentences.zh: 杨白做的事情非常简单。

sentences.en: She had people at that moment draw themselves and write me.
sentences.zh: 她让人们在那个时刻画下自己并写下“我”。

sentences.en: And in that context, those drawings of the self were really small.
sentences.zh: 在这种背景下，那些关于自我的画作真的很小。

sentences.en: They wrote their sense of me really small compared to the right kind of control conditions.
sentences.zh: 与适当的对照条件相比，他们写下的“我”的感知非常小。

sentences.en: And we have other data and really different kinds of data, even neuroscientific data showing,
sentences.zh: 我们还有其他数据，以及完全不同类型的数据，甚至是神经科学的数据表明，

sentences.en: awe quiets this egoistic, self-focused sense of personal identity and opens you up to the big things that you're connected to.
sentences.zh: 敬畏能够平息这种自私的、以自我为中心的个人认同感，让你向与你相连的宏大事物敞开心扉。

sentences.en: You and your collaborator, Lani Shioda, also once had people stand in front of an enormous T-Rex skeleton.
sentences.zh: 你和你的合作者拉尼·シオダ（Lani Shioda）也曾让人们站在一具巨大的霸王龙骨架前。

sentences.en: Tell me about that experiment, Dakar.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲那个实验吧，达克尔。

sentences.en: On the Berkeley campus, we have this incredible replica of a T-Rex skeleton.
sentences.zh: 在伯克利校园里，我们有这具令人难以置信的霸王龙骨架复制品。

sentences.en: And it's in our Museum of Paleontology.
sentences.zh: 它在我们的古生物学博物馆里。

sentences.en: And you stand next to it.
sentences.zh: 你就站在它旁边。

sentences.en: And we did the pilot testing.
sentences.zh: 我们进行了预先测试。

sentences.en: People say, I feel awe, man.
sentences.zh: 人们说，天哪，我感到敬畏。

sentences.en: This is amazing.
sentences.zh: 这太惊人了。

sentences.en: It's huge.
sentences.zh: 它太巨大了。

sentences.en: Imagine being chased by that thing, you know?
sentences.zh: 想象一下被那东西追赶是什么感觉，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Wow!
sentences.zh: 哇！

sentences.en: Those things existed 70 million years ago?
sentences.zh: 那些东西在7000万年前就存在了？

sentences.en: It's awesome!
sentences.zh: 太棒了！

sentences.en: So, Lonnie and our team stood Berkeley undergraduates by this T-Rex, or they stood in the opposite
sentences.zh: 所以，罗妮和我们的团队让伯克利本科生站在这个霸王龙旁边，或者让他们面向相反的

sentences.en: direction looking down a hallway.
sentences.zh: 方向看着一条走廊。

sentences.en: And there's this classic measure of your own self or identity, which is you are given the
sentences.zh: 这里有一个经典的衡量你自我或认同感的标准，就是给你一个

sentences.en: stem, I am, and next to it is a blank line, and you just fill it in 20 different times.
sentences.zh: 词干“我是”，旁边是一条空白线，你只需连续20次填空。

sentences.en: And typically, people living in the West will say things like, I am, you know, extroverted,
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，生活在西方的人会说这样的话：我是，你知道的，外向的，

sentences.en: and I am ambitious, and I am interested in this.
sentences.zh: 我是雄心勃勃的，我对这个很感兴趣。

sentences.en: And when they stood next to that T-Rex and took it in and felt awe, their sense of self expanded,
sentences.zh: 而当他们站在那只霸王龙旁边吸收这种感觉并感到敬畏时，他们的自我感扩大了，

sentences.en: and themes of common humanity emerged.
sentences.zh: 共同的人性主题浮现出来。

sentences.en: I am a human.
sentences.zh: 我是人。

sentences.en: I am a mammal.
sentences.zh: 我是哺乳动物。

sentences.en: I am a part of California.
sentences.zh: 我是加利福尼亚的一部分。

sentences.en: I am of this ethnic variety.
sentences.zh: 我属于这种族裔。

sentences.en: And so this collective, communal self emerged.
sentences.zh: 于是，这种集体的、群体的自我浮现了。

sentences.en: And that's the power of awe.
sentences.zh: 这就是敬畏的力量。

sentences.en: A little moment, 30 seconds of it, you shift from self-focus, very narrow, to, wow, I'm part of something really large.
sentences.zh: 短短的一小会儿，30秒的时间，你就从非常狭隘的自我关注，转变为了，哇，我是某个非常宏大事物的一部分。

sentences.en: And some of this translates not just to how we think about ourselves in our own minds, but how we're acting towards other people.
sentences.zh: 其中一些不仅转化为了我们如何在自己心中看待自己，还转化为了我们如何对待他人。

sentences.en: You also ran another experiment on the Berkeley campus, this time involving a grow of eucalyptus trees.
sentences.zh: 你还在伯克利校园里进行了另一项实验，这次涉及一片桉树林。

sentences.en: Tell me about that study, Ducker.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲那项研究吧，达克尔。

sentences.en: Yeah, you know, one of the beauties of awe, and to understand it, it brings out the best of our imagination, you know.
sentences.zh: 是的，你知道的，敬畏的美妙之处之一，为了理解它，它激发了我们想象力的最好部分，你知道的。

sentences.en: And my lab started to get interested in awe, and we were throwing around all these ideas and doing these crazy studies.
sentences.zh: 我的实验室开始对敬畏产生兴趣，我们到处抛出各种想法，并做着这些疯狂的研究。

sentences.en: And the very imaginative Paul Piff, now a professor at UC Irvine, did a study in which he took undergrads to a eucalyptus grove.
sentences.zh: 极具想象力的保罗·皮夫（Paul Piff，现为加州大学欧文分校教授）做了一项研究，他带本科生去了一个桉树林。

sentences.en: And they're blue gum eucalyptus trees.
sentences.zh: 那是蓝胶桉树。

sentences.en: They're some of the tallest in North America.
sentences.zh: 它们是北美最高的树木之一。

sentences.en: When you look up into them, their light and the colors and the leaves and their fragrances are just astonishing.
sentences.zh: 当你抬头仰望它们时，它们的光线、色彩、树叶以及散发的芳香简直令人惊叹。

sentences.en: That grove, when you stand in the middle of them, embraces you.
sentences.zh: 当你站在它们中间时，那片树林拥抱着你。

sentences.en: It makes you feel like you're part of them.
sentences.zh: 它让你觉得你是它们的一部分。

sentences.en: And in the control condition, people are in the same place, but they looked at this science building.
sentences.zh: 而在对照条件下，人们在同一个地方，但他们看着这栋科学大楼。

sentences.en: And lo and behold, you know, Shankar, this is a minute or two of just for no reason looking up into these trees.
sentences.zh: 你看，香卡，这只是一两分钟无缘无故地抬头看着这些树。

sentences.en: In one to two minutes, our students reported feeling less narcissistic, less entitled.
sentences.zh: 在一到两分钟内，我们的学生报告说，他们感觉不那么自恋了，不那么觉得理所当然了。

sentences.en: They needed less money to do the study when we offered to pay them.
sentences.zh: 当我们提议付钱时，他们做研究所需的报酬也变少了。

sentences.en: And then Paul staged this accident where a student was walking by, and they dropped some pens.
sentences.zh: 然后保罗策划了一场意外，一个学生走过，掉了一些笔。

sentences.en: And the people feeling awe picked up more pens, right?
sentences.zh: 感到敬畏的人捡起了更多的笔，对吧？

sentences.en: And we replicated that in tightly controlled laboratory studies.
sentences.zh: 我们在严密控制的实验室研究中复制了这一点。

sentences.en: You just share more when you're feeling awe.
sentences.zh: 当你感受到敬畏时，你就会分享更多。

sentences.en: You cooperate more.
sentences.zh: 你更懂得合作。

sentences.en: You give more.
sentences.zh: 你给予得更多。

sentences.en: Just with a minute or two of looking up at some trees.
sentences.zh: 只需花一两分钟抬头看看一些树。

sentences.en: You know, very much like you described about your own experiences in Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，非常类似于你所描述的你在威斯康星州的亲身经历。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You and Jonathan Haidt have said that an experience of awe can press a reset button in the mind.
sentences.zh: 你和乔纳森·海特（Jonathan Haidt）曾说过，体验敬畏可以按下大脑中的重置按钮。

sentences.en: What do you mean by that, Dakar?
sentences.zh: 你这话是什么意思，达克尔？

sentences.en: Reset buttons are really interesting.
sentences.zh: 重置按钮真的很有趣。

sentences.en: And actually, you know, Sylvan Tompkins wrote about when you're startled by a loud clap of thunder or the appearance of an old friend or bumping into a friend in the street.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你知道的，西尔van·汤普金斯（Sylvan Tomkins）曾写过，当你被一声响亮的雷鸣吓到，或者老朋友突然出现，又或者在街上偶遇朋友时。

sentences.en: It kind of restarts your mind.
sentences.zh: 它有点像重新启动你的大脑。

sentences.en: It resets it to look at things anew and fresh and contemplative people might say with a beginner's mind.
sentences.zh: 它将其重置，以便以崭新的、新鲜的、用contemplative（沉思的）人们可能会说是带着初学者的心态去看待事物。

sentences.en: And that's what awe does for a Shankar.
sentences.zh: 这就是敬畏为香卡所做的事情。

sentences.en: When we come back, how to bring more awe into our lives.
sentences.zh: 广告回来后，我们将探讨如何将更多的敬畏带入我们的生活。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 您正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: At UC Berkeley, psychologist Dakar Keltner studies the benevolent emotions, including the emotion of awe.
sentences.zh: 在加州大学伯克利分校，心理学家达克尔·凯尔特纳（Dakar Keltner）研究仁慈的情绪，包括敬畏情绪。

sentences.en: He's the author of the book, Awe, The New Science of Everyday Wonder and How It Can Transform Your Life.
sentences.zh: 他是《敬畏：日常惊奇的新科学以及它如何改变你的生活》一书的作者。

sentences.en: Dakar, you recently studied the effects of awe on disadvantaged students and military veterans.
sentences.zh: 达克尔，你最近研究了敬畏对弱势学生和退伍军人的影响。

sentences.en: Neither felt much awe in their regular lives.
sentences.zh: 他们在日常生活中都感觉不到太多的敬畏。

sentences.en: What did you do?
sentences.zh: 你们做了什么？

sentences.en: What did the study involve?
sentences.zh: 这项研究包含哪些内容？

sentences.en: Yeah, you know, there's a growing interest in our culture and scientifically about how the institutional structural traumas of life,
sentences.zh: 是的，你知道的，我们的文化和科学界对以下问题越来越感兴趣：生活的制度性结构创伤，

sentences.en: if you're impoverished and you don't have parks nearby and the like, or you have a career like veterans who go see combat and see people die.
sentences.zh: 如果你身处贫困，附近没有公园之类的场所，或者你从事像退伍军人那样去经历战斗并看着战友死去的职业。

sentences.en: Their profiles look traumatized.
sentences.zh: 他们的状况看起来受到了创伤。

sentences.en: They are depressed and vigilant, anxious very often, twice the rates of American citizens, elevated levels of cortisol and inflammation and the like.
sentences.zh: 他们抑郁、高度警惕、经常焦虑，其比例是美国公民的两倍，皮质醇和炎症等水平也有所升高。

sentences.en: And I became friends with Stacy Bear, who's a veteran, and we started talking about this.
sentences.zh: 我和斯黛西·贝尔（Stacy Bear）成为了朋友，他是一名退伍军人，我们开始谈论这个。

sentences.en: And he leads veterans into outdoors prograMs.
sentences.zh: 他带领退伍军人参加户外项目。

sentences.en: And so what we decided to do in this study is we got veterans and high school students who were in really tough, impoverished schools in parts of the East Bay in California.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在这项研究中决定做的是，我们找来了退伍军人和高中生，他们来自加州东湾地区一些条件非常艰苦、贫困的学校。

sentences.en: And it's, you know, where there are bars and police cars and no gardens, etc.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，那里到处都是酒吧和警车，没有花园等等。

sentences.en: And these kids hadn't, you know, been outside in parks.
sentences.zh: 这些孩子以前从来没有去过公园。

sentences.en: They hadn't gone camping.
sentences.zh: 他们没有去露营过。

sentences.en: Many of them had not really seen a night sky of stars.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人甚至从未真正见过满天繁星的夜空。

sentences.en: So we took them rafting our veterans and then our high schoolers down the American River on a stretch.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们带着我们的退伍军人和高中生在美利坚河的一段河面上进行了一次漂流。

sentences.en: And it's beautiful.
sentences.zh: 景色非常美。

sentences.en: And you you wind through these rapids and you look at the water and you see fish and it's amazing.
sentences.zh: 你在急流中穿行，看着水流，看着鱼儿，感觉太奇妙了。

sentences.en: And what we found, we measured their emotions and stress and trauma and sense of connection at the start of the study a week later.
sentences.zh: 我们在研究开始时以及一周后，测量了他们的情绪、压力、创伤和连接感。

sentences.en: And as the study unfolded, we measured their sense of wonder and awe and connection to their peers and cortisol and emotions.
sentences.zh: 随着研究的进行，我们测量了他们对惊叹、敬畏、同伴连接感、皮质醇以及情绪的感受。

sentences.en: And what we found is our high schoolers a week later felt less stress, more happiness.
sentences.zh: 结果我们发现，一周后，我们的高中生压力更小，感到更多快乐。

sentences.en: They felt more connected to their community and family.
sentences.zh: 他们感到与社区和家庭的联系更加紧密。

sentences.en: And our veterans felt 30 percent less PTSD.
sentences.zh: 而我们的退伍军人的创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）减轻了百分之三十。

sentences.en: One high schooler said, I'm so struck by the rolling hills and the smoke.
sentences.zh: 一个高中生说：“我被连绵起伏的山丘和烟雾深深震撼了。”

sentences.en: And it was smoky at the time because of wildfires and the water.
sentences.zh: 当时由于野火和水面，到处都是烟雾。

sentences.en: And then a veteran said, and I love this quote where, you know, the star splatted sky made me realize that my worries are not as important as I thought they are.
sentences.zh: 接着一位退伍军人说——我非常喜欢这句话——“星光点缀的天空让我意识到，我的烦恼其实并没有我想象的那么重要。”

sentences.en: But what I could do in the world is more important.
sentences.zh: 而我在世界上能做的事情才更重要。

sentences.en: And so it was this nice study.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个很好的研究。

sentences.en: And there's a lot of science on this of different varieties that nature immersion and finding awe, gardening, walking, getting out into the woods,
sentences.zh: 关于这方面有许多不同种类的科学研究：大自然沉浸、寻找敬畏、园艺、散步、走进树林，

sentences.en: standing near a tree is good for your nervous system and your mind.
sentences.zh: 站在树旁对你的神经系统和心灵都有好处。

sentences.en: Is there any evidence that awe has physiological effects on us?
sentences.zh: 有没有什么证据表明敬畏对我们的生理产生影响？

sentences.en: Yeah, there are, you know, there's this thing called the vagus nerve, largest bundle of nerves in your body.
sentences.zh: 是的，有的，你知道的，有个东西叫迷走神经，它是你体内最大的神经束。

sentences.en: It slows heart rate, deepens breathing, regulates digestion, helps with your gut and the microbiome.
sentences.zh: 它能减缓心率、加深呼吸、调节消化，对肠道和微生物群有益。

sentences.en: In general, people who have a nice functioning vagus nerve that is responsive and has elevated levels do better in life.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，那些拥有运转良好、反应灵敏且迷走神经水平较高的人，生活得更好。

sentences.en: And we found, thanks to Amy Gordon and Jenny Stellar, you know, that little brief experiences of awe, seeing an inspiring image, hearing about moral beauty,
sentences.zh: 多亏了艾米·戈登（Amy Gordon）和珍妮·斯特拉（Jenny Stellar），我们发现，短暂的敬畏体验——看到一张鼓舞人心的图片，听到关于道德美的故事——

sentences.en: elevates your vagus nerve activation.
sentences.zh: 能提升你的迷走神经激活水平。

sentences.en: And then, just as impressively, you know, when your immune system, the cytokine system more specifically, cranks out these proteins that attack pathogens.
sentences.zh: 同样令人印象深刻的是，当你的免疫系统，更具体地说是细胞因子系统，产生这些攻击病原体的蛋白质时。

sentences.en: And that's the inflammation response that makes you feel feverish and sluggish and overheated.
sentences.zh: 这就是炎症反应，它会让你感到发烧、疲惫和身体发热。

sentences.en: It's good when you're fighting a virus.
sentences.zh: 当你对抗病毒时，这是好事。

sentences.en: It's not good if you're chronically inflamed.
sentences.zh: 但如果你长期处于炎症状态，这就不是好事了。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And it's one of the central threats to health in the United States.
sentences.zh: 这也是美国健康面临的核心威胁之一。

sentences.en: And Jenny Stellar and Neha John Henderson went out and found in our lab that feeling a lot of awe of all the positive emotions quiets down the inflammation response.
sentences.zh: 珍妮·斯特拉和内哈·约翰·亨德森（Neha John Henderson）在我们的实验室发现，在所有积极情绪中，体验到强烈的敬畏感可以平息炎症反应。

sentences.en: So it tells us, you know, Emerson, when he had this big epiphany of awe out on a cold day in Massachusetts, he said, there is nothing that nature cannot repair.
sentences.zh: 这就告诉我们，正如爱默生在马萨诸塞州一个寒冷的日子里产生这种重大的敬畏顿悟时所说：“没有什么能大自然无法修复。”

sentences.en: And I think he was feeling these changes in the body of vagal tone and inflammation, reduced inflammation, that awe gives us.
sentences.zh: 我想他当时感受到了身体内部迷走神经张力和炎症的变化——炎症的减少——这是敬畏带给我们的。

sentences.en: So, Dr., you've described many ways in which awe is good for us, but you've also said that our society is becoming awe-deprived.
sentences.zh: 那么，教授，您描述了敬畏对我们有益的许多方式，但您也说过我们的社会正变得缺乏敬畏。

sentences.en: What do you mean by that?
sentences.zh: 您这是什么意思？

sentences.en: The deeper structural conditions of our lives are, in some ways, especially for young people today, working against awe.
sentences.zh: 我们生活的深层结构条件在某些方面正在消解敬畏，尤其是对当今的年轻人而言。

sentences.en: And I really sense this teaching thousands of students a year at a big university like Berkeley.
sentences.zh: 在伯克利这样的大学里每年教导数千名学生，我对此有着深刻的感受。

sentences.en: They are awe-deprived because too much is structured and they are not allowed to wander, like I did as a kid, wandering around the neighborhoods and out in the foothills.
sentences.zh: 他们缺乏敬畏，因为生活被规划得太满了，他们不被允许像我小时候那样在街区和山麓间四处游荡。

sentences.en: They are awe-deprived because of the new technologies, which frankly just get us too focused on the self.
sentences.zh: 他们由于新技术的出现而缺乏敬畏，坦率地说，这些技术让我们过度关注自我。

sentences.en: The more we're focused on the self, the narrow parts of the self, the less awe we feel.
sentences.zh: 我们越是关注自我、关注狭隘的自我部分，我们感受到的敬畏就越少。

sentences.en: They are awe-deprived because of all the competitive self-comparisons that have arisen today.
sentences.zh: 由于当今出现的所有好胜的自我对比，他们缺乏敬畏。

sentences.en: So are people getting enough of it?
sentences.zh: 那么人们获得的敬畏足够吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不够。

sentences.en: We need more awe right now.
sentences.zh: 我们现在需要更多的敬畏。

sentences.en: You know, Lancet publication recently showed that the pandemic has led to rises in depression and anxiety by 20 to 30 percent.
sentences.zh: 你知道，最近《柳叶刀》发表的一项研究表明，大流行导致抑郁和焦虑水平上升了百分之二十到三十。

sentences.en: We've all felt this, our young people in particular.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都感受到了这一点，尤其是我们的年轻人。

sentences.en: But there is everyday awe.
sentences.zh: 但生活中处处都有日常的敬畏。

sentences.en: And if we just take a little moment to get out and look for it, it's there to find.
sentences.zh: 如果我们花一点时间走出去寻找它，它是随处可寻的。

sentences.en: So, Dacher, in one recent study, you had volunteers take an awe walk.
sentences.zh: 达彻，在最近的一项研究中，你让志愿者进行了一次“敬畏漫步”。

sentences.en: What is an awe walk?
sentences.zh: 什么是“敬畏漫步”？

sentences.en: One of the easiest ways to find awe is to, in an unbounded way, go out and walk.
sentences.zh: 寻找敬畏最简单的方法之一，就是以一种不受束缚的方式走出去散步。

sentences.en: We have been doing this as humans for a long time in the spiritual contemplative traditions.
sentences.zh: 作为人类，我们在精神冥想传统中已经这样做了很长时间。

sentences.en: Getting out into nature and doing awe walks is just part of those traditions.
sentences.zh: 走进大自然并进行敬畏漫步正是这些传统的一部分。

sentences.en: And what we decided to do is test its benefits scientifically.
sentences.zh: 我们决定通过科学的方法来检验它的益处。

sentences.en: And so I wrote up these instructions for an awe walk.
sentences.zh: 于是我写下了这些关于敬畏漫步的说明。

sentences.en: And what you do is you take your ordinary walk that a lot of people do.
sentences.zh: 你要做的是进行许多人都会进行的普通散步。

sentences.en: And in fact, during the pandemic, there were historic levels of walking.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在大流行期间，散步达到了历史最高水平。

sentences.en: And you not only go out to do it vigorously and to help your heart, but you go with a childlike sense of wonder.
sentences.zh: 你不单是为了充满活力地锻炼和有益心脏而走，还要带着一种孩童般的惊叹感去走。

sentences.en: And you just stop and reflect on what is really interesting in the small things around you.
sentences.zh: 你只需要停下来，思考你身边那些微小事物中真正有趣的东西。

sentences.en: The flowers and patterns of shadows and the like.
sentences.zh: 花朵、阴影的图案等等。

sentences.en: And also look up past the horizon and look up to the vast things, right?
sentences.zh: 同时，还要把目光投向地平线以上，去仰望那些宏大的事物，对吗？

sentences.en: And do it in a way where you go places that you're curious about.
sentences.zh: 以这种方式去你感到好奇的地方。

sentences.en: And in this study, what we did is our participants were all 75 years old or older.
sentences.zh: 在这项研究中，我们的参与者年龄都在75岁或以上。

sentences.en: That is an age where, because we have a sense that death is coming and we see people die,
sentences.zh: 在这个年龄段，因为我们感觉到死亡正在逼近，而且我们看到人们离去，

sentences.en: we're a little bit more anxious at that stage of life.
sentences.zh: 我们在人生的那个阶段会感到更加焦虑。

sentences.en: And so one group of our participants did an awe walk once a week for eight weeks.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们的一组参与者每星期进行一次敬畏漫步，持续八周。

sentences.en: The other group of participants, tight control, did a vigorous walk once a week.
sentences.zh: 作为严格的对照，另一组参与者每星期进行一次常规的活力健步走。

sentences.en: Each time they did a walk, they took a picture of themselves.
sentences.zh: 每次散步时，他们都会给自己拍张照片。

sentences.en: And then we gathered a bunch of self reports, like how are they doing on a daily basis?
sentences.zh: 然后我们收集了大量自我报告，比如他们日常过得怎么样？

sentences.en: How is their levels of anxiety and so forth?
sentences.zh: 他们的焦虑水平如何，诸如此类？

sentences.en: And we found just a couple of things.
sentences.zh: 我们发现了几个结果。

sentences.en: One, the more you do the awe walk, the more awe-inspiring it becomes.
sentences.zh: 第一，你进行敬畏漫步的次数越多，它带来的敬畏感就越强。

sentences.en: Awe doesn't diminish with experience.
sentences.zh: 敬畏并不会随着经验而减少。

sentences.en: It gets richer and deeper.
sentences.zh: 它变得更丰富、更深厚。

sentences.en: By the end of the eight weeks, our awe walk participants were feeling a lot of awe.
sentences.zh: 到八周结束时，参加敬畏漫步的参与者感受到了强烈的敬畏感。

sentences.en: Two, more changes in the self.
sentences.zh: 第二，自我发生了更多改变。

sentences.en: They're pictures of themselves.
sentences.zh: 这是他们自己的照片。

sentences.en: And I love this finding.
sentences.zh: 我非常喜欢这个发现。

sentences.en: The self gets smaller over time.
sentences.zh: 随着时间推移，自我变得越来越小。

sentences.en: And it starts to drift off to the side.
sentences.zh: 并且开始退居一旁。

sentences.en: And they're including, you know, the rocks and sunsets of their awe walk.
sentences.zh: 他们把敬畏漫步中的岩石和日落也融入了自我认知中。

sentences.en: And then third, really importantly, on a daily basis, they just felt less distress.
sentences.zh: 第三，非常重要的一点是，在日常生活中，他们的痛苦感减少了。

sentences.en: You know, they felt less anxiety about life.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们对生活的焦虑感降低了。

sentences.en: You know, in many ways in this conversation, Dakar,
sentences.zh: 达彻，在这次谈话的许多方面，

sentences.en: we've spent a lot of time talking about awe in the beautiful and the majestic.
sentences.zh: 我们花了大量时间讨论关于美丽和壮丽事物的敬畏。

sentences.en: But you've written that so much of life is awesome, including the parts that are not great.
sentences.zh: 但你曾写道，生活中的许多事物都令人敬畏，包括那些并不美好的部分。

sentences.en: Tell me about your relationship with your brother, Rolf.
sentences.zh: 跟我聊聊你和你的兄弟罗尔夫（Rolf）的关系吧。

sentences.en: You were very close to him, right?
sentences.zh: 你们以前非常亲密，对吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, you know, just hearing you say his name brings goosebumps and tears to me.
sentences.zh: 是的，你知道的，一听到你叫他的名字，我就起鸡皮疙瘩，眼泪夺眶而出。

sentences.en: He was born one year after me, so he was younger.
sentences.zh: 他比我小一岁，所以他是弟弟。

sentences.en: And we did everything together.
sentences.zh: 我们一起做所有事情。

sentences.en: We played Little League together.
sentences.zh: 我们一起打少年棒球联赛。

sentences.en: We played basketball teams together, wandered together, went to Mexico together,
sentences.zh: 我们一起加入篮球球队，一起四处游荡，一起去墨西哥，

sentences.en: were best men in each other's weddings.
sentences.zh: 在彼此的婚礼上担任伴郎。

sentences.en: We both became social science-y teacher types.
sentences.zh: 我们俩都成了偏向社会科学的老师类型。

sentences.en: And frankly, he taught me how to be kinder and how to be courageous.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，是他教会了我如何更善良、如何变得勇敢。

sentences.en: I don't think I was endowed with those tendencies early.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我早年并没有这些天生倾向。

sentences.en: He taught me.
sentences.zh: 是他教导了我。

sentences.en: He was my example in many ways of moral beauty.
sentences.zh: 在许多方面，他是我道德美的榜样。

sentences.en: So I was profoundly close to him through the ebbs and flows of brotherhood.
sentences.zh: 因此，在兄弟情谊的起起伏伏中，我和他有着极深的羁绊。

sentences.en: But he was my core.
sentences.zh: 但他是我内心的核心。

sentences.en: So I understand a few years ago he was diagnosed with colon cancer.
sentences.zh: 我听说几年前他被诊断出患有结肠癌。

sentences.en: Tell me about that, Dakar.
sentences.zh: 达彻，能跟我讲讲那件事吗？

sentences.en: Anyone out listening, you know, who's been close to colon cancer, it's a horror show.
sentences.zh: 任何听节目的朋友，如果曾经亲近过结肠癌患者，就会知道那简直是一场噩梦。

sentences.en: And for my brother, for two years I watched him, you know, go from being a 210 pound, very strong man, 147 pounds, bone thin, passing out.
sentences.zh: 对于我的兄弟，我看着他在两年里从一个210磅、非常强壮的男子变成147磅、骨瘦如柴、频频昏厥。

sentences.en: There's a lot of pain, but there are certain kinds of pain that just wipe out consciousness, break through pain.
sentences.zh: 有很多疼痛，但有些疼痛会直接摧毁意识、突破对痛觉的感知。

sentences.en: And abdominal pain is like that.
sentences.zh: 腹痛就是这种感觉。

sentences.en: He got it all.
sentences.zh: 他把这些都经历了一遍。

sentences.en: Chemotherapy.
sentences.zh: 化疗。

sentences.en: And I was just there all the time.
sentences.zh: 我一直都陪在他身边。

sentences.en: And then he decided to take a cocktail when he knew the cancer had returned and headed into his gut.
sentences.zh: 后来，当他得知癌症复发并转移到肠道时，他决定接受安乐死药物（cocktail）。

sentences.en: And we all went up there in January and we watched him, you know, slowly leave this world.
sentences.zh: 我们在1月都赶了过去，看着他慢慢离开这个世界。

sentences.en: And Shankar, I had gone through the most horrifying two years of my life watching my companion in awe, my brother Rolf, fade physically.
sentences.zh: 尚卡尔（Shankar），我经历了我一生中最可怕的两年，看着我的敬畏同伴、我的兄弟罗尔夫身体日渐消瘦。

sentences.en: But in that moment of seeing him calmer, heading into where he was going after losing his body, we were all around him.
sentences.zh: 但在看到他变得更加平静、在失去肉体后走向他该去的地方的那一刻，我们都围绕在他身边。

sentences.en: We touched him.
sentences.zh: 我们触摸着他。

sentences.en: The light felt different.
sentences.zh: 光线感觉不一样了。

sentences.en: We were quiet.
sentences.zh: 我们保持着安静。

sentences.en: We bowed our heads.
sentences.zh: 我们低下了头。

sentences.en: And we were all in reverence of my brother Rolf and what he meant.
sentences.zh: 我们全都在对我的兄弟罗尔夫以及他所代表的意义表达崇敬。

sentences.en: And watching him go, I was filled with astonishment and awe.
sentences.zh: 看着他离去，我心中充满了惊奇与敬畏。

sentences.en: I understand that you took a trip to honor your brother's memory after he died.
sentences.zh: 我听说在他去世后，你进行了一次旅行来缅怀他的记忆。

sentences.en: Where did you go, Dakar?
sentences.zh: 达彻，你去哪里了？

sentences.en: After he died, and then I returned to my life in Berkeley and was blown off the map.
sentences.zh: 在他去世后，我返回伯克利继续生活，却感觉世界崩塌了。

sentences.en: And it's really the state that Joan Didion describes, you know, in her writing about grief.
sentences.zh: 这真的是琼·狄迪恩（Joan Didion）在关于悲伤的写作中所描述的那种状态。

sentences.en: I couldn't sleep and anxious and confused and was just really struggling.
sentences.zh: 我无法入眠，感到焦虑和迷茫，生活举步维艰。

sentences.en: And this voice came to me and it was find awe.
sentences.zh: 然后一个声音在我脑海中响起：去寻找敬畏。

sentences.en: And my brother and I, we always went to the mountains.
sentences.zh: 我和我兄弟以前总是去山里。

sentences.en: You know, we grew up in the mountains near the Sierras.
sentences.zh: 我们在内华达山脉附近的群山中长大。

sentences.en: And I went up into the high Sierras and Ducks Lake where he and I had hiked, and Mammoth in the east side of the Sierras.
sentences.zh: 我去了内华达山脉的高处和鸭子湖（Ducks Lake），我和他曾在那儿徒步，还有内华达山脉东侧的猛犸山（Mammoth）。

sentences.en: When I saw the ridge line that he and I had seen, I felt him there.
sentences.zh: 当我看到我和他曾看过的山脊线时，我感觉他在那里。

sentences.en: I heard his voice.
sentences.zh: 我听到了他的声音。

sentences.en: I saw the trees that he and I had seen.
sentences.zh: 我看到了我和他曾见过的那些树木。

sentences.en: These trees flicker in the wind, the aspen trees.
sentences.zh: 这些树在风中摇曳，那是白杨树。

sentences.en: And I just felt him there, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 尚卡尔，我就是觉得他在那里。

sentences.en: I was like, in these mountains, my brother is with me.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，在这群山之中，我的兄弟与我同在。

sentences.en: Dakar Keltner is a psychologist at the University of California, Berkeley.
sentences.zh: 达彻·凯尔特纳（Dacher Keltner）是加州大学伯克利分校的心理学家。

sentences.en: He's the author of Awe, the new science of everyday wonder and how it can transform your life.
sentences.zh: 他是《敬畏：日常惊奇的新科学以及它如何改变你的生活》（Awe: The New Science of Everyday Wonder and How It Can Transform Your Life）一书的作者。

sentences.en: Dakar, thank you for joining me today on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 达彻，谢谢你今天做客《隐藏的大脑》（Hidden Brain）。

sentences.en: Shankar, it is a privilege to be in conversation with you.
sentences.zh: 尚卡尔，能与你对话是我的荣幸。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: Hidden Brain is produced by Hidden Brain Media.
sentences.zh: 《隐藏的大脑》由 Hidden Brain Media 制作。

sentences.en: Our audio production team includes Bridget McCarthy, Annie Murphy-Paul, Kristen Wong, Laura Querell, Ryan Katz, Autumn Barnes, and Andrew Chadwick.
sentences.zh: 我们的音频制作团队包括布里奇特·麦卡锡（Bridget McCarthy）、安妮·墨菲-保尔（Annie Murphy-Paul）、克里斯滕·王（Kristen Wong）、劳拉·克雷尔（Laura Querell）、瑞恩·卡茨（Ryan Katz）、奥秋姆·巴恩斯（Autumn Barnes）和安德鲁·查德威克（Andrew Chadwick）。

sentences.en: Tara Boyle is our executive producer.
sentences.zh: 塔拉·博伊尔（Tara Boyle）是我们的执行制片人。

sentences.en: I'm Hidden Brain's executive editor.
sentences.zh: 我是《隐藏的大脑》的执行主编。

sentences.en: As many of you know, we recently started a new show called My Unsung Hero.
sentences.zh: 正如你们许多人所知，我们最近开办了一个新节目，名叫《我无名无姓的英雄》（My Unsung Hero）。

sentences.en: It's designed to show you that the world is filled with everyday acts of kindness and courage.
sentences.zh: 它的旨在向你展示，这个世界充满了日常的善良与勇敢行为。

sentences.en: As I've listened to stories of unsung heroes, I've often found myself moved to tears.
sentences.zh: 当我听着这些平凡英雄的故事时，我常常感动得热泪盈眶。

sentences.en: But it wasn't until I talked to Dakar that I realized these are really stories about moral beauty.
sentences.zh: 但直到我与达彻交谈后，我才意识到这些其实都是关于道德美的故事。

sentences.en: The reason these stories make me want to be a better person?
sentences.zh: 这些故事让我想要成为一个更好的人的原因是什么？

sentences.en: They're giving me a feeling of awe.
sentences.zh: 它们给予了我一种敬畏感。

sentences.en: Please subscribe to the My Unsung Hero podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 请订阅《我未被传颂的英雄》播客。

sentences.en: Here's a taste of what it's like.
sentences.zh: 以下是节目内容的精彩片段。

sentences.en: This story comes from Ali Ward.
sentences.zh: 这个故事来自阿里·沃德。

sentences.en: In 2013, Ali's life felt like it was collapsing.
sentences.zh: 2013年时，阿里的生活感觉像是要崩溃了。

sentences.en: Her relationship with her partner fell apart.
sentences.zh: 她与伴侣的关系破裂了。

sentences.en: Her new job wasn't working out.
sentences.zh: 她的新工作并不顺利。

sentences.en: And her father was diagnosed with a rare form of cancer.
sentences.zh: 而且她的父亲被诊断出患有一种罕见的癌症。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, my dad's brother had the same kind of cancer and died.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，我爸爸的兄弟也得了同一种癌症并去世了。

sentences.en: And there was a lot going on.
sentences.zh: 当时有太多的事情压在心头。

sentences.en: I remember days when I would think I only cried four times today.
sentences.zh: 我记得有些日子，我会想我今天只哭了四次。

sentences.en: That was a good day for me.
sentences.zh: 对我来说那就算是个好日子了。

sentences.en: It was just really tough.
sentences.zh: 那段日子真的非常艰难。

sentences.en: It was a lot of things that I just couldn't help.
sentences.zh: 有很多事情是我根本无能为力的。

sentences.en: When she needed a distraction, Ali liked to go on Facebook and post pictures of her unconventional obsession.
sentences.zh: 当需要转移注意力时，阿里喜欢登录Facebook，发布她那些非主流爱好的照片。

sentences.en: Bugs, worms, spiders, brightly colored beetles.
sentences.zh: 昆虫、蠕虫、蜘蛛、色彩鲜艳的甲虫。

sentences.en: Her close friends found it endearing, but in Los Angeles, where she lived, not everyone got it.
sentences.zh: 她的密友觉得这很讨人喜欢，但在她生活的洛杉矶，并不是每个人都能理解。

sentences.en: There's, you know, a little bit of artifice in LA and you don't find a lot of people that get excited about a spider web.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，洛杉矶多少有点虚浮，你很难找到一群会对蜘蛛网感到兴奋的人。

sentences.en: One day, she got a Facebook message from a friend of a friend, a woman she had never met named Leela Higgins.
sentences.zh: 有一天，她收到了一位朋友的朋友发来的Facebook消息，那是一个她从未见过名叫莉拉·希金斯的女人。

sentences.en: Leela was an entomologist at the local Natural History Museum, and she had noticed Ali's quirky bug pictures.
sentences.zh: 莉拉是当地自然历史博物馆的昆虫学家，她注意到了阿里那些古怪的昆虫照片。

sentences.en: So she reached out.
sentences.zh: 于是她主动联系了她。

sentences.en: And she said, I heard you like bugs.
sentences.zh: 她说，我听说你喜欢昆虫。

sentences.en: If you want to come check, there's this insectary in the middle of like the catacombs, the inner workings of the museum.
sentences.zh: 如果你想来看看的话，在地下墓穴般的博物馆内部深处，有一个昆虫饲养室。

sentences.en: Just come and check out some bugs.
sentences.zh: 随时来参观一些昆虫吧。

sentences.en: Leela had no idea what I was going through in my life at that time.
sentences.zh: 莉拉当时根本不知道我生活中正在经历什么。

sentences.en: I think she probably didn't expect someone jittery and tear stained to meet her at the back door of this museum.
sentences.zh: 我想她大概没料到，在博物馆后门迎接她的会是一个神情紧张、满脸泪痕的人。

sentences.en: But this is my jam.
sentences.zh: 但这正合我意。

sentences.en: I have loved bugs since I was a little kid.
sentences.zh: 我从小就对昆虫喜爱有加。

sentences.en: There is nothing I wanted more than to see some scorpions and some larvae.
sentences.zh: 我最大的愿望就是能看看蝎子和幼虫。

sentences.en: I was like, I would love this.
sentences.zh: 当时我就想，我太乐意了。

sentences.en: And I went and was just delighted by it.
sentences.zh: 于是我去了，并为此欣喜若狂。

sentences.en: I got to put on a lab coat.
sentences.zh: 我穿上了实验室白大褂。

sentences.en: I got to go through some secret doors, some employee only areas.
sentences.zh: 我穿过了一些秘密门，进入了员工专属区域。

sentences.en: And I remember she opened up this freezer, like, come check this out.
sentences.zh: 我记得她打开了这个冰柜，就像是说，快来看看这个。

sentences.en: And then just the freezer opening like a coffin.
sentences.zh: 然后那个冰柜像棺材一样打开了。

sentences.en: And it was full of dead bugs, dead tarantulas, some stick insects.
sentences.zh: 里面装满了死去的昆虫、死去的狼蛛和一些竹节虫。

sentences.en: I mean, big scorpions.
sentences.zh: 我是说，还有大蝎子。

sentences.en: I mean, all kinds of things that have passed away, but they were saving them for the entomology department or just for posterity.
sentences.zh: 我是说，各种各样已经死去的生物，但它们被留作昆虫学部门的研究之用，或者只是为了流传后世。

sentences.en: And I just remember just how excited she was about everything was such a pass for me to get excited about this in her company and really rediscover what excited me in life.
sentences.zh: 我只记得她对所有东西都那么兴奋，这给了我极大的许可，让我也能在她的陪伴下为这些感到兴奋，并真正重新发现了生活中让我激动的事物。

sentences.en: You know, at the end, she said, you should volunteer here.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，最后她说，你应该来这里做志愿者。

sentences.en: And I remember, I mean, I was like in between crying Jags that day.
sentences.zh: 我记得，我的意思是，那天我正处在痛哭流涕的间隙中。

sentences.en: And I was like, how could my life get a lot worse?
sentences.zh: 当时我想，我的生活还能怎么变得更糟呢？

sentences.en: I can afford three hours a week.
sentences.zh: 我每周还是能抽出三个小时的。

sentences.en: So I started volunteering and I just would really light up.
sentences.zh: 于是我开始做志愿者，整个人都焕发了生机。

sentences.en: It gave me this like sense of purpose.
sentences.zh: 这给了我一种使命感。

sentences.en: It helped me reconnect with my love of science and nature that I'd always had.
sentences.zh: 它帮我重新找回了对科学和自然一直以来的热爱。

sentences.en: You know, Lila Higgins just in one instant changed my whole life.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，莉拉·希金斯就在转瞬之间改变了我的一生。

sentences.en: And I think that she's impacted a lot of lives that she probably doesn't understand.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为她影响了许多她可能自己都意料到的生命。

sentences.en: You know, I think that it's just in a day's work for her to point out snails and slugs and butterflies and, you know, mosey on, keep doing her job.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我认为对她来说，指出蜗牛、蛞蝓、蝴蝶并继续前行、做好她的工作，不过是日常工作的一部分。

sentences.en: And I don't think that she understands the ripple effect that she has.
sentences.zh: 我不认为她明白她所产生的涟漪效应有多大。

sentences.en: She has caused like such an exponential effect, I think, in my life.
sentences.zh: 我认为她在我的生活中造成了如此巨大的指数级影响。

sentences.en: I felt like I came home to myself because of the way that that she can be herself.
sentences.zh: 因为她能够做真实的自己，我也感觉自己终于找回了真正的自我。

sentences.en: Ali Ward lives in Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 阿里·沃德住在洛杉矶。

sentences.en: Since she quit that job she didn't like, she has started her own science podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 自从她辞去了那份不喜欢的工作后，她创办了自己的科学播客。

sentences.en: It's called Ologies.
sentences.zh: 节目名叫《Ologies》。

sentences.en: If you found our Happiness 2.0 series useful and inspiring, please take a moment and tell a friend or colleague about our show.
sentences.zh: 如果你觉得我们的“幸福2.0”系列有用且富有启发，请花一点时间向朋友或同事推荐我们的节目。

sentences.en: Think of one person who might enjoy our program and tell them about it.
sentences.zh: 想出一个可能会喜欢我们节目的人，并把节目介绍给他们。

sentences.en: Another way you can support us is by supporting us.
sentences.zh: 你可以支持我们的另一个方式就是支持我们本身。

sentences.en: Help us build more shows like this by going to support.hiddenbrain.org.
sentences.zh: 请访问 support.hiddenbrain.org，帮助我们制作更多这样的节目。

sentences.en: Again, that's support.hiddenbrain.org.
sentences.zh: 再重复一遍，网址是 support.hiddenbrain.org。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: See you soon.
sentences.zh: 我们不久后见。
